# discipline — situational hard rules

Each part is a trigger-first micro contract: load the one matching the
situation, follow its rules literally, ignore the rest. They are kept as
separate parts (not merged) so the trigger conditions stay precise.

## Parts

| Part | Load when |
|---|---|
| `parts/agent-refactor-safety/` | About to refactor/split a monolith, extract modules, merge project versions, delete imports/functions, move changes between projects |
| `parts/changelog-discipline/` | Maintain/update/create a CHANGELOG as a decision log: after changes, release prep |
| `parts/jsonc-surgical-edit/` | Edit JSON/JSONC configs programmatically WITHOUT losing comments and formatting |
| `parts/cross-platform-gotchas/` | Writing/editing cross-platform scripts or installers (Python/bash, Linux/macOS/Windows) |
| `parts/testing-discipline/` | Add/fix tests, determine "is it done", reproduce a bug with a test, verify limits/rejections |
| `parts/debug-incident-protocol/` | "Doesn't work", "still broken", "hung", "disappeared after update", "metric is zero but UI OK" |
| `parts/money-path-safety/` | Any debit/credit/quota logic: pay/buy/subscribe, bonuses, refunds, balance checks |
| `parts/production-first-decisions/` | ANY "how to do it" decision: approach/tool/library choice, "what if" scenarios, new mechanisms |
| `parts/architecture-simplicity/` | Design/redesign modules and layers, library-vs-own-code, "why is this a god-file", adding abstraction |
| `parts/hardening-observability/` | Harden service limits/protection, add metrics/logs/alerts, fix "metrics lie" |

## How to use

1. Match the situation against the "Load when" column — the descriptions in
   each part carry the full trigger list.
2. Load only that part and follow it. Do not read the others.
3. When two parts match (e.g. refactor + money path), load both; they do not
   conflict.
